text:
incident_bot: PAGER: 🚨 Automatic multi-region traffic-shift failed for route group `frontend-prod`. Multiple health checks failing in eu-west-2 during DR run. Impact: ~30% of users hitting eu-west-2 report 502/timeout. @prod_oncall paging.
prod_oncall: Acked. I'm on it, joining the call now. Can someone confirm if this is a control-plane-only issue or data-plane?
sre_maya: Jumping in — initial telemetry shows route flips from eu-west-2 -> us-east-1 are timing out at the load-balancer layer; backend pods in us-east-1 are healthy. Looks like DNS + connection tear-downs, not app crashes.
net_alex: We're seeing a spike in TCP RSTs from eu-west-2 egress. Possible AZ-level networking flap. Cloud provider has an open maintenance advisory for eu-west-2b ~10m ago.
prod_oncall: @net_alex good call. Can we pause the automatic traffic-shift so we don't keep flipping patients?
sre_maya: Yes — executing: `redwood infra traffic-shift pause --group frontend-prod --reason "az flap eu-west-2"`
deploy_bot: deploy-bot: traffic-shift pause accepted by controller (id=ts-7623). Canary window canceled.
engliaison_john: Noted for customers on the runbook. I'll send a short update to the incident page and start tickboxes for customer impact.
support_zoe: Getting complaints from a few enterprise customers reporting slow API calls on EU nodes. One customer reported token rejections after 502s. I'm collecting request IDs.
prod_oncall: Priority mitigation plan: 1) Pause traffic-shift (done). 2) Force drain of eu-west-2 endpoints to take them out of LB rotation. 3) Lower DNS TTL for affected records to 30s to accelerate fallback if needed. 4) Escalate to cloud provider with flow logs + packet captures.
net_alex: Starting forced drain: `kubectl -n redwood patch svc frontend --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/metadata/annotations/drain","value":"true"}]'` — watch for 503->504 transition.
sre_maya: I see backend connection pools still holding connections to eu-west-2 for ~45s — lowering idle timeout on proxy layer to 15s: `cfg set proxy.pool_idle=15s`
prod_oncall: Do we have any in-flight migrations or model cache rebuilds that would be disrupted by draining?
engliaison_john: No large model caches in progress for frontend-prod. A few embedding jobs in DEPRECATED queue, won't affect user-facing API.
support_zoe: Customer A (acct: 21498) saw 502s at 12:03Z, sent logs. I forwarded request ids to @sre_maya.
sre_maya: Received, correlating. Preliminary: 502s all map to the same LB instance in eu-west-2 that lost health.
net_alex: Cloud provider support: Case #CLOUD-8921 opened. They acknowledge degraded network connectivity within eu-west-2 with packet loss ~10-15% between AZs. No ETA yet. Asking for routing plane status.
prod_oncall: Given provider ETA uncertain, let's create a controlled regional failover to eu-central-1 for EU traffic as a backup. Steps: update routing policy to prefer eu-central-1, but keep us-east-1 as global fallback.
sre_maya: Creating new routing policy: `infra route update --group frontend-prod --policy prefer:eu-central-1,then:us-east-1` — preview shows ~82% of EU queries will go to eu-central-1. Executing now.
deploy_bot: deploy-bot: routing policy change queued (id=rp-334). Will apply after canary window 30s.
prod_oncall: Canary applied. Monitoring metrics.
net_alex: After canary, RTT to eu-central-1 is fine. No packet loss.
sre_maya: Error budget alert suppressed for this failover. Watching 5xx and p50/p95 latency on frontend-prod.
support_zoe: Messaging for customers: short update sent out to affected accounts explaining temporary failover to eu-central-1 and potential ~200-400ms latency bump for a subset. :email:
engliaison_john: I'll add a note to the status page: "Latency spike and partial errors in EU region due to cloud AZ network flap; traffic shifted to eu-central-1 as mitigation."
prod_oncall: Handoff note for next on-call (@sre_maya -> @engliaison_john): 1) Cloud provider case open; update every 15m. 2) Keep traffic-shift paused; routing policy set to prefer eu-central-1. 3) Continue draining eu-west-2; do not re-enable until provider clears network. 4) Support to escalate any major customer impact.
sre_maya: Handoff ack. I'll be on the call for 10 more minutes then hand off final notes.
net_alex: Also: we adjusted DNS TTLs to 30s for `*.frontend.redwood.ai` (applied). Remember to revert TTL bump after incident.
sre_maya: Quick runbook snippet I used: ```
# quick check list
1. pause auto-shift
2. force-drain region
3. set routing preference
4. lower DNS TTL
5. escalate to CP
6. monitor 5xx and latency
```
prod_oncall: Any customer-facing action beyond Zoe's emails? Legal/Trust wants a post-incident summary if >10% customers affected. Current estimate is <5% impacted with transient errors, so flagging as P1 but not legal.
engliaison_john: I'll draft a brief postmortem skeleton and include timeline + mitigation steps.
support_zoe: Confirm: are we running health-check sweeps for all AZs in eu-west-2 to detect recovery before returning traffic?
sre_maya: Yes — enabling additional health probes with shorter intervals: `healthctl probe --region eu-west-2 --interval 10s`
incident_bot: NOTE: Pager silenced for prod_oncall during handoff window (30m).
prod_oncall: Closing this thread for immediate mitigation steps. Next updates will be posted in the incident doc and via case #CLOUD-8921. Handing off to @engliaison_john for customer comms and long-tail monitoring.
engliaison_john: Handoff acked. I'll post a summary and set a follow-up review in 3 hours. Please ping me if provider gives ETA earlier. :thumbsup:
